clue.text: Firm on strike is in serious trouble

blocks.note: firm and hard both mean solid, unyielding
to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: A company facing industrial action finds itself in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' and 'strike' look like a business and a walkout, but they are an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone badly affected by a blow, such as a recession, is described as hard-hit, meaning suffering heavily.

blocks.note: first meaning: a kick at the shins, as in rugby or football
second meaning: an ordinary riding horse, often a hired one

explanation.surface: Someone receives a kick from a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a horse's kick, but the horse and the kick are each a separate meaning of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both striking a player's shins with the foot and a plain riding animal kept for hire.

clue.text: Badly delivered over to knock about

indicators.note: something delivered badly arrives in the wrong state, so the letters come out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler sends down a poor over and it gets hit around.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by a bowler, which is why 'delivered over' reads so naturally; knock about means wander here, not hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock about is an informal way to say wander aimlessly from place to place, which is what roving means.

blocks.note: surface reading: a gathering of non-clergy, ordinary church members
setter's reading: a gathering of birds that lay eggs, the females of the poultry yard, which names a pre-wedding party for a bride and her women friends

explanation.walkthrough: Lay looks like the churchy adjective meaning not ordained; read it as what the females of the farmyard do.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration held for a bride-to-be with her female friends is named after female chickens, the birds that lay eggs.

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: At a harbour, a single item is loaded into barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: The roman numeral I sits inside TUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tunisia is a Mediterranean seaport city on the North African coast.

clue.text: They cut some of the grass

blocks.note: first meaning: the sharp edges of knives or razors
second meaning: individual leaves of a lawn

explanation.surface: A mower trims part of the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about mowing, but it splits into two separate meanings of the same plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Knife edges do the cutting, and the slender leaves of a lawn plant are called by the same plural noun.

blocks.note: surface reading: pastries such as apple turnovers in a coating of batter or crumbs
setter's reading: the folded-back flaps on the front of a jacket below the collar

explanation.walkthrough: Turnovers suggests pastries and coats suggests a coating; really they are the turned-back parts of a jacket front.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the folded flaps on a jacket front that continue from the collar, literally turned over.

blocks.note: surface reading: a way of getting commissions as an artist
setter's reading: fasten a sketch to a board or wall

explanation.walkthrough: Secure seems to mean obtain, as in landing a job; here it means fix in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbtack, used for pinning paper sketches to boards, takes its British name from that artistic use.

blocks.note: surface reading: a striking garment or piece of jewellery
setter's reading: making an impression, as a seal pressed into wax

explanation.walkthrough: Impressive means stunning in the surface; literally it means able to leave an impression, which a seal on a finger does in wax.
explanation.definitionFit: This finger jewellery carries an engraved seal used to stamp wax, so it literally makes impressions.

clue.text: Contract is unable to include the cooker

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: unable means cannot, contracted to can't
an oven is a cooker or part of one

explanation.surface: A deal falls through because the kitchen appliance won't be part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords ignore apostrophes, so a contraction like the one for unable can be used as plain letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal binding agreement between parties, often a legal deed, is a synonym for a contract.

clue.text: Telephoned after the odds leapt up

indicators.note: coming after places the telephone word behind the odds word in the answer

blocks.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
telephoned means rang someone up

explanation.surface: Someone phoned once the betting odds were announced, and they shot up.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds on a horse when a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang is the past tense of spring, which means to jump or leap suddenly upward.

clue.text: I'm mounting new raid above ground level

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so the word is read from bottom to top
something new has been made afresh, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot climbs into the sky for a fresh bombing attack.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so a word that is mounting reads upward, which turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up in the sky, clear of the earth and not yet landed, is said to be in mid-air.

clue.text: The strain of the French Revolution

definitions.text: The strain of the French Revolution

blocks.clueFragment: The strain of the French Revolution
blocks.note: surface reading: the stress and pressure France suffered during the Revolution
setter's reading: a strain is a tune, so this is the song of the revolutionaries

explanation.walkthrough: Strain seems to mean stress; it also means a piece of music, here the revolutionary song that became France's national anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: The national anthem of France was composed in 1792 and sung by revolutionary volunteers from the southern port city.

blocks.note: surface reading: a noisy worker who keeps people awake at night
setter's reading: the wooden or concrete beams under railway lines, which a track worker shifts

explanation.walkthrough: Sleepers are the cross-beams supporting railway rails, called railroad ties in America; the British track maintenance worker lays and moves them.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway labourer who lays and maintains track works on the rails and beams the trains run over.

clue.text: Safety rail adapted for the nursery?

definitions.note: describes the answer's use rather than naming it; the answer is a plural noun

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered to suit, so these letters are refashioned

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cot's protective barrier is modified for a child's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the stories are things meant for the nursery, the room where young children are read to.
explanation.definitionFit: Magical stories of princesses and goblins are traditionally told to small children at bedtime in their playroom.

clue.text: Sort of lady we hate to precede

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so these words are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A certain kind of woman we dislike always pushes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To go first and guide the others behind is to go before them, a verb phrase synonym.

indicators.note: something that has gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles from the famous London clock tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling off' wants to be read together as the definition; 'off' is the anagram signal. Big Ben is the great bell in the Westminster clock tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbing is the sea level going down, so ebbing describes a decline or fall.

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: a lark or prank, as in a student rag

explanation.surface: A songbird is magically transformed into a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lark looks like the bird, but here it means a prank; a rag is a British student prank or charity stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The garfish is a long slender fish with a needle-like beak, sometimes called needlefish.

clue.text: Is he in the orchestra, or dismissed?

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: an orchestra is a band of musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether a musician is still playing or has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: IS HE goes inside BAND, splitting it as BAN-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished has been sent away or expelled, so dismissed in the sense of ordered to leave.

definitions.note: the second meaning is the substance a cigarette may be low in

blocks.note: first meaning: a seaman, an old word for a sailor
second meaning: the tobacco residue that cigarettes are labelled low in

explanation.surface: A seaman may be running short of smokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Low in cigarettes suggests running out; read it as the phrase 'low-tar' on a cigarette packet.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is old slang for a seaman, and the sticky residue of smoked tobacco is what mild cigarettes contain little of.

indicators.note: something shocked is jolted out of place, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Passengers are alarmed by a fault found during the flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A deviation from what is normal or correct, such as a flaw in a lens, is a kind of fault.

clue.text: Unseated, we hear, from seat of power

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the spelling may differ from the sound

blocks.note: a rider unseated from a horse has been thrown

explanation.surface: A ruler is ousted from office.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial chair stands for royal authority, so it is literally where power sits.

clue.text: Have a great time - never mind the tears?

blocks.note: first meaning: act without restraint and enjoy yourself fully
second meaning, read cryptically: allow objects to tear, not caring about rips

explanation.walkthrough: Tears suggests crying, but the rhyme-free word here is the other tear, a rip in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means abandoning restraint and having fun, and literally it means allowing items to be torn.

blocks.note: S, E, N, S and E are compass points, each a way or direction

explanation.surface: There are lots of means of expressing emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are crossword shorthand for directions, so 'ways' gives single letters N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch, sight and hearing are each a faculty of perception, so a feeling is one of them.

clue.text: Qualifying for an attendance mark in the register

definitions.note: the answer is what a pupil says to qualify, i.e. being present

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A pupil earns a tick on the school roll by turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: being present earns the mark, and it is also the very word pupils answer at roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present in the room is what earns the tick, and pupils answer their name at roll call with this word.

indicators.note: doing something wrong means doing it incorrectly, so these letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A misbehaving pupil is punished with lines to write out.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines suggests the school punishment of copying a sentence; here it means verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems are made of verse, so poetry is loosely called lines in crosswords.

blocks.note: first meaning: the hue of a lemon or a canary
second meaning: cowardly, inclined to flee danger

explanation.surface: A dye that bleeds in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: Run suggests dye bleeding in the wash; it means running away.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the shade of lemons and, as slang, describes a cowardly person who flees from danger.

clue.text: Finally need hint, perhaps, to solve this clue

indicators.note: perhaps marks one possible version, so these letters may be arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver admits that eventually a clue will be required.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at last, after everything else has happened, as an adverbial expression of eventual outcome.

blocks.note: first meaning: hurtles forward, as a bull does
second meaning: unedited daily prints of footage

explanation.surface: A list of fees for first prints of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Charges looks like fees; it is the verb, to dash at.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurtling forward is to charge, and filmmakers call the unedited daily prints of footage by this plural noun.

blocks.note: surface reading: describing the jeweller's band set with stones all the way round
setter's reading: any circle has no terminus, just as eternity never stops

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to want a jewellery term; it wants an adjective true both of eternity and of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle has no start or finish, and eternity never stops, so both are without limit.
